objective: Improve geometric-mean full and incremental JavaScript, Rust, and Python parsing throughput using the operation and bytes/sec semantics of crates/cli/benches/benchmark.rs. Exact full and edited trees, exact changed ranges, incremental/full equivalence, parser tests, and per-workload peak RSS no greater than the frozen baseline plus 2% are hard gates. Only lib/src is mutable.

terminalSeal.corpusExposure: capsule directory and admission evidence only; never inserted into optimizer corpus or panel evidence

meta.license: MIT; upstream Tree-sitter and all three pinned grammar LICENSE files preserved
meta.provenance: tree-sitter/tree-sitter at exact revision 1ffd612be56259938c47507bbe953af739c7f640. Grammar fixtures are vendored protected assets from tree-sitter-javascript v0.25.0 (44c892e0be055ac465d5eeddae6d3e194424e7de), tree-sitter-rust v0.24.0 (18b0515fca567f5a10aee9978c6d2640e878671a), and tree-sitter-python v0.23.6 (bffb65a8cfe4e46290331dfef0dbf0ef3679de11). Deterministic generated source workloads contain no third-party corpus text. The trusted harness preserves the Parser::parse repetition and bytes/sec semantics of crates/cli/benches/benchmark.rs and adds deterministic TSInputEdit incremental parses. qReference is frozen after interleaved terminal A-A as qBase + max(5*sigma, 0.05*abs(qBase-qFail)). Fastest-of-five reference-normalized fresh-process A-A samples [50666505.29794153, 51955609.6264734, 51102086.23932623, 50809293.91475852, 51566649.62333815, 50522360.646954104] across two consecutive ordering passes give sigma=557825.1604303756, with qBase=50661657.83045164 fixed by the frozen yardstick scale, and qReference=53450783.63260352.

sourceDetails.declaredBaselineConstruction: synthetic admission baseline committed on top of the pinned upstream revision: the upstream tree reduced to the capsule envelope plus the trusted evaluator glue (eval.py, harness.c, benchmark.rs, challenge.json, toolchain.lock.json); the upstream commit is the sole parent and remains the provenance anchor
sourceDetails.toolchain: GCC 12.2.0 and Python 3.11.2 on pinned Debian linux/arm64
sourceDetails.offlineDependencies: all runtime, generated grammar C sources, workloads, tests, and build tools are vendored or image-pinned; evaluator network disabled

measurement.platform: Docker Desktop Linux arm64 on Apple M3 Max; provisional local terminal calibration
measurement.q: geometric mean across 12 full/incremental language-size cells of the fastest-of-five per-phase candidate/reference time ratio, multiplied by the frozen scale 50661657.83045164; the reference is a trusted in-eval baseline yardstick built from /trusted/baseline sources and run interleaved with the candidate inside the same evaluation
measurement.benchSampling: per workload: trusted-reference and candidate bench repetitions interleaved seconds apart on the same trusted per-repetition schedule seed, one warm repetition each, then five timed repetitions with each phase scored from its minimum nanoseconds for candidate and reference alike (trusted trimmed sampling; timing noise is strictly additive and not candidate-controlled, and the interleaved in-eval yardstick divides out drift shared across evaluations); every warmup and timed iteration parses identity-distinct schedule-variant content (class-preserving alphanumeric byte swaps dispersed across the whole buffer) so cached or replayed trees from any other iteration are structurally wrong, and each timed tree's full pre-order signature digest must equal the in-eval trusted reference run on the same seed; byte counters re-verified against the sealed workload on every repetition; RSS gate uses the maximum candidate peak across all repetitions
measurement.rssGate: GNU time wait4 peak workload RSS <= frozen same-workload baseline RSS * 1.02; baselines frozen over the schedule-variant harness with ten samples per workload
measurement.correctness: SHA-256 exact original/edited trees, exact changed ranges, incremental equals fresh full parse, and error-free parser tests

exploitReview.protectedPathEscape: broker protects evaluator, harness, headers, metadata, image, assets, and all paths outside lib/src; evaluator independently reconstructs protected files from /trusted/baseline and rejects symlinks/non-regular files and new files outside lib/src
exploitReview.benchmarkSpecialCasing: separate all-holdout train and validation splits; shortcut diagnostic fingerprints the train prefix, wins train, and is forced below baseline on validation
exploitReview.fixtureFingerprinting: workload and expected-tree assets are root-only broker mounts; compilation completes as uid 2000 before workload bytes are copied into the runnable build directory; protected validation is independently measured
exploitReview.outputFabrication: trusted harness invokes the real C runtime API, serializes real trees, checks incremental/full equality, and emits verdicts and counters only after every parse succeeds through direct pinned linux/arm64 write syscalls with in-harness integer formatting, so candidate objects linked into the same executable cannot interpose libc output symbols; the evaluator independently recomputes both byte counters from the sealed workload sizes, edit deltas, and trusted iteration counts and rejects any disagreement, and additionally requires the candidate's per-phase timed-tree signature digests to equal those of the trusted in-eval reference binary run on the same schedule seed; evaluator hashes trusted harness files
exploitReview.timerTampering: trusted harness reads CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW with a direct pinned linux/arm64 kernel syscall, and failure exits use a direct exit_group syscall, bypassing candidate-linked symbols; compiler flags, harness, iterations, scalarizer, and GNU-time RSS supervisor are protected; prlimit blocks candidate forks and evaluator processes run unprivileged
exploitReview.buildScriptMutation: no candidate build script executes; trusted evaluator invokes pinned cc commands on lib/src and protected grammar sources with network disabled
exploitReview.deadCodeBenchmarkBypass: the same ts_parser_parse_string API and language parsers produce exact-tree/parser-test evidence immediately before the timed phases, and every timed full and incremental call parses identity-distinct schedule-variant content whose full pre-order tree signature is digest-checked against the trusted in-eval reference run, so replaying, caching, or skipping timed parses cannot reproduce the required digests
